thesis: An eight-mana commander with haste and trample printed on him is the whole engine: reach eight mana (three, if Otepec Huntmaster, Urza's Incubator and Knight of the Stampede are all down), connect once, and the reveal free-rolls Dinosaurs off the top into a layer of per-Dinosaur-entry payoffs that pay the reveal back in cards and a discover — the enrage web that used to be a second engine is now a two-card residue whose damage comes from Blasphemous Act, Zacama's activation, Itzquinth's entry or a blocker, and the deck lives or dies on whether Gishath connects.

stages.label: THE EIGHT-MANA CLIMB
stages.what_it_does: Pays for a {5}{R}{G}{W} commander and a curve whose fat end is 11 five-drops and 14 cards at six or more counting the commander (deck-facts curve: 6:7, 7:2, 8:2, 9:2, 12:1; 13 without Gishath). 35 land copies across 24 entries, 12 of which enter tapped; land sources by colour are G 22 / R 18 / W 17 against a source target of 36 each (deck-facts mana), so Gishath's three pips are the binding constraint, not his generic five. Four rocks, three land-ramp sorceries, and six permanents that make outsized mana or lands on a board: Mirari's Wake and Regal Behemoth double a tapped land, Selvala taps for the greatest power on your board, Hulking Raptor adds {G}{G} every first main, Topiary Stomper searches a basic onto the battlefield tapped when it enters, and Wayward Swordtooth adds a land drop. The goldfish reads mean available mana 5.96 on turn 6 and 7.527 on turn 8 (goldfish_metrics), and the 'Ramp or fixing drawn' target (thirteen cards, Knight of the Stampede now among them) assembles in 96.4% of games, 86.4% by turn 6, mean turn 2.335. Two lands carry restricted mana: Unclaimed Territory pays creature spells of the chosen type only — it pays Gishath and cannot pay Rogue's Passage or Kessig Wolf Run — while Secluded Courtyard's clause says 'or activate an ability' and does (deck-facts notes). Forge V3 (40 games): Sol Ring cast 10, Skyshroud Claim 9, Talisman 8, Mirari's Wake 7, Selvala 7, Wayward Swordtooth 10, Boros Signet 0 for 2 discards (sim engine_casts).

stages.label: THE FIRST CONNECTION
stages.what_it_does: Gishath has to resolve and deal combat damage to a player. Nothing else in the deck does its thing until that happens, and he needs no help to attack: 'Vigilance, trample, haste' is his own text. What the kit does is make the cast earlier and the hit bigger. Three cost reducers touch a command-zone cast — Otepec Huntmaster ({1} less), Urza's Incubator ({2}) and Knight of the Stampede ({2}) — and they pay generic only, so all three together leave exactly {R}{G}{W}. Rogue's Passage makes him unblockable for {4}; Kessig Wolf Run adds +X/+0; Enlarge is +7/+7 and trample with 'must be blocked this turn if able', so fourteen is the unblocked ceiling and the reveal against a blocker is what tramples over; Kinjalli's Sunwing taps a flashed-in blocker; Sunfrill Imitator attacking beside him may become a second 7/6 with the reveal trigger (unverified — open question). Priced from the brief: commander mean cast turn 7.362, median 7, cast by turn 6 in 25.5% of games, never by turn 10 in 2,299 of 10,000; the modelled reveal fired in 7,255 games, 1.953 times a game, for 4.096 free Dinosaurs, at a connect rate of 0.70 per attack that is Forge's, not the model's (goldfish_metrics commander_reveal; the source is the V3 record: 60 attacks, 42 triggers). Forge V3 cast Gishath 49 times in 40 games, activated Rogue's Passage 10 times and Kessig 3, cast Otepec 11 and Incubator 3 (sim engine_casts). The 'Cost reducer or cheat-into-play drawn' target reads 81.0% assembled, 64.1% by turn 6, mean turn 3.334 for seven cards — but four of the seven cannot touch a command-zone cast (see proposed_goldfish_edits).

evidence.note: the trigger resolving on a real board: reveal seven, put every Dinosaur creature card among them onto the battlefield as one event, the rest to the bottom in random order

stages.label: WHAT THE TOP OF THE LIBRARY HOLDS
stages.what_it_does: The reveal converts only Dinosaur creature cards, so fuel is density plus arrangement plus the doors that skip the cast. Density: 30 of the deck's 34 creature entries are Dinosaurs by type line (cards.json); the four that are not — Huatli, Knight of the Stampede, Otepec Huntmaster, Selvala — bottom when revealed. Arrangement: Congregation at Dawn puts three creatures on top in your order, Worldly Tutor one, Enlightened Tutor an artifact or enchantment (Garruk's Uprising, Descendants' Path, Urza's Incubator, Belbe's Portal are all legal finds). Doors: Descendants' Path casts a Dinosaur free off the top every upkeep you control one, Belbe's Portal and Monster Manual put one from hand onto the battlefield for {3} or {1}{G}, Huatli's Saga makes two 3/3 Dinosaurs, tutors a third, then grants double strike; Etali and Bonehoard Dracosaur are free spells off other tops. Hand refill: Hunter's Insight and Rishkar's Expertise draw off power, Runic Armasaur off opponents' activations. Goldfish extra cards drawn by turn 8: 1.353 (turn 10: 3.147), with 2 of 8 draw cards modelled and Hunter's Insight, Runic Armasaur, Selvala, Vaultborn and Curious Altisaur named unmodelled (goldfish_metrics card_advantage). Forge V3 is a FLOOR here: Rishkar's Expertise and Hunter's Insight are absent from the engine_casts block — never cast, never discarded, in 40 games — while Monster Manual was cast 7 and activated 7, Belbe's Portal cast 3 / activated 2, Descendants' Path cast 6, Bonehoard 15, Etali 2, Congregation 5, Worldly Tutor 6, Enlightened Tutor 5. The V3 record cannot speak to Runic Armasaur, which was not on the list.

stages.label: A CARD PER DINOSAUR
stages.what_it_does: What turns a Dinosaur entering, or connecting, into something other than a body. Per entry: Pantlaza discovers X = that creature's toughness, once a turn; Garruk's Uprising and Vaultborn Tyrant draw for each entering creature with power 4 or more (Vaultborn also gains 3); Earthshaker Dreadmaw draws one per other Dinosaur when it lands. Per connection: Curious Altisaur draws when any Dinosaur deals combat damage to a player, Quartzwood Crasher makes an X/X where X is the trample damage dealt. Stack 001 is the fact tier: four Dinosaurs off one seven-card reveal enter as ONE event, so Uprising triggers three times (the 3/4 misses), Pantlaza triggers four times and discovers exactly once, and the pilot orders the Regisaur token trigger to the bottom so the token cannot re-trigger Pantlaza. Three of the stack's seven stipulated reveal cards (Ripjaw Raptor, Cultivate, Ravenous Sailback) are not in the current 99 — Sailback never was — and of the four Dinosaurs it put onto the battlefield, Regisaur Alpha and Carnage Tyrant remain; the rules facts do not depend on which Dinosaurs are revealed. The enrage residue: Trapjaw Tyrant exiles an opponent's creature whenever it is dealt damage, Wrathful Raptors redirects any damage a Dinosaur of yours takes at a non-Dinosaur — stack 004 resolves four redirects for 16 off one Blasphemous Act. Priced: 'Dinosaur payoff drawn' 84.9% assembled, 60.4% by turn 6, mean turn 3.985 for six cards (Vaultborn and Dreadmaw not in the group); 'Enrage engine drawn' 56.7%, 28.1% by turn 6, mean turn 5.705, size 2, thin. Forge V3: Garruk's Uprising cast 7, Pantlaza 6, Curious Altisaur 6, Quartzwood 6, Vaultborn 5, Wrathful 7, Trapjaw 5 (sim engine_casts).

evidence.note: three Uprising draws and one discover at X=6 off four simultaneous entries; the once-per-turn rider restricts triggering (603.2h), which is why the token ordering matters

stages.label: WHAT THE BODIES DO ON ARRIVAL
stages.what_it_does: Removal and targeted actions, two-thirds of it riding on Dinosaurs the reveal can put down for free. Read the cast-gates before counting on a revealed body: Wakening Sun's Avatar destroys all non-Dinosaurs only 'if you cast it from your hand', and Zacama untaps your lands only 'if you cast it' — off the reveal both are bodies with activated or no text, though Zacama's {2}{R} 3-damage and {2}{G} artifact/enchantment modes still work, and Forge V3 activated Zacama 32 times against one cast. Bronzebeak Foragers' exile-per-opponent, Trumpeting Carnosaur's discover 5 and Itzquinth's pay-{2} hit — a Dinosaur you control deals its power to another target creature, one way, any creature, your own Trapjaw or Wrathful included — are plain ETBs and fire off the reveal. Blasphemous Act is the one-sided sweeper: {R} off nine creatures, 13 to everything, one-sided only through Temple Altisaur (stack 004). deck-audit's single point of failure is scoped to that pair, 'THE ONE-SIDED APOCALYPSE: Blasphemous Act + Temple Altisaur' — the Act alone is 7.1% of an opening seven; the pair reads 8.1% assembled, 1.8% by turn 6, mean turn 7.708 (29.9% tutor-assisted). The stage loses nothing else it does without the Act, and the enrage residue has other ways to be dealt damage: Zacama's activation, Itzquinth, Carnosaur's discard mode, Triumphant Chomp and a blocker. Chomp scales with your biggest Dinosaur's power. Path, Swords, Beast Within and Austere Command clear the lane before the connection. Forge V3: Swords 11, Path 10, Triumphant Chomp 8, Itzquinth 7, Blasphemous Act 6, Austere Command 4, Bronzebeak 4, Brontodon 4, Wakening 2, Beast Within 1; Trumpeting Carnosaur cast once, discarded 6, activated 5 — the AI used the discard mode (sim engine_casts).

stages.label: KEEPING THE BOARD THROUGH THE ANSWER
stages.what_it_does: Five instants and one Dinosaur. Heroic Intervention (hexproof and indestructible), Flawless Maneuver (indestructible, free if you control your commander), Akroma's Will (the same plus evasion on the other mode), Boros Charm (indestructible — or double strike on one creature, which on Gishath is a second reveal) and Eerie Interlude, which exiles your creatures in response and returns them at the next end step, re-firing every ETB in the conversion and output stages at once (unverified — open question). Temple Altisaur is a prevention shield, not insurance: 'prevent all but 1' of any damage to ANOTHER Dinosaur you control, which is what turns Blasphemous Act one-sided; stack 004 confirms Altisaur is not 'another Dinosaur' to itself, eats the full 13 and dies, and its death still redirects 13 through Wrathful Raptors by last known information. Priced: 'Protection held for the board' 70.0% assembled, 51.1% by turn 6, mean turn 3.846; interaction castable with mana left over 35.1% on turn 6, a floor since the model casts everything it can (goldfish_metrics). Forge V3: Boros Charm cast 9, Flawless Maneuver 7, Akroma's Will 5, Eerie Interlude 5, Heroic Intervention 4, Temple Altisaur 4 (sim engine_casts).

evidence.note: prevention applies as the damage is dealt (615.1): 13 becomes 1 for each other Dinosaur, and 1 is still 'dealt damage' for the triggers
WRATH INSURANCE holds four of the five instants; its fifth member is Carnage Tyrant, a hexproof body that insures itself and is placed under wincon here

stages.label: THE TRAMPLE SWING
stages.what_it_does: Combat, with trample stacked from every direction. Overwhelming Stampede gives the board +X/+X and trample where X is your greatest power — Gishath alone makes X at least 7; Ghalta, Primal Hunger costs {G}{G} off any board the reveal built and swings for 12; Ghalta and Mavren makes an X/X trampler tapped and attacking every swing, X the greatest power among the other attackers; Regal Imperiosaur is +1/+1 to every other Dinosaur; Regisaur Alpha gives the arriving board haste, so a Dinosaur that enters precombat (Descendants' Path at upkeep, a Portal or Manual activation in main one) attacks the same turn — stack 001 shows the reveal's own bodies cannot, since they land after attackers were declared. Carnage Tyrant and Pugnacious Hammerskull are the bodies with nothing to do but hit: 7/6 hexproof uncounterable, and a 6/6 for three that stuns itself only when it is your lone Dinosaur. Priced with model_combat on, one opponent, no blockers: kill by turn 6 5.8%, turn 7 29.3%, turn 8 61.7%, turn 10 90.5%, mean kill turn 8.03, median 8, no kill by turn 10 in 9.5%; mean board power 31.555 on turn 8 and 55.571 on turn 10 (goldfish_metrics combat). Forge V3 against sythis / jarad / abaddon: 12 wins of 35 decided, 0.343 (sim summary). No checker-passed stack resolves a lethal swing; the closest is stack 004's 16 redirected damage, explicitly not lethal. Forge V3: Ghalta cast 10, Carnage Tyrant 9, Overwhelming Stampede 8, Hammerskull 8, Imperiosaur 7, Ghalta and Mavren 6, Regisaur Alpha 1 (sim engine_casts).

map_disagreements.why: engine-facts' scatter table puts 'Ramp or fixing drawn' across four cities: the rocks cluster on 'add mana', the land sorceries and Topiary Stomper on 'search your library', while the four mana creatures read as what they are on the battlefield — Regal Behemoth and Wayward Swordtooth as Dinosaurs, Hulking Raptor and Selvala beside Belbe's Portal and Monster Manual in THE SIDE DOOR. A creature that makes mana is filed as a creature; the job is invisible in the text.

Gishath clusters with Etali and Bonehoard on 'play from the top' text, Enlarge, Kinjalli's Sunwing and Sunfrill Imitator on board-scaling text, his three cost reducers with Blasphemous Act on 'costs less', and his evasion with the lands. Nothing in card text says 'these make one attack happen'; the connection is a board event, which is exactly what a clustering over oracle text cannot see.

Trapjaw Tyrant clusters on its exile text among the removal, while Wrathful Raptors clusters with the Dinosaur mass; the two remaining enrage converters share a trigger condition and no city. The residue is invisible on the map because it is small and its members read as other things.

map_disagreements.component: KEEPING THE BOARD THROUGH THE ANSWER (protection)
map_disagreements.why: Temple Altisaur is a prevention effect that reads as a Dinosaur, and Eerie Interlude a blink that reads as recursion; both land in city-0 hood-1 while the four instants that do the same job sit in city-4 with Carnage Tyrant, a body that insures itself and belongs to the wincon here.

The deck's one verified pairing outside the reveal has two addresses: Blasphemous Act is filed with Otepec, Incubator and Knight on its 'costs {1} less' clause, and Temple Altisaur, the card that makes it one-sided, is in city-0 hood-1 with Wrathful Raptors. The cartographer's own note says not to describe city-6 as the wipe; stack 004 is the only place the pair is visible together.

open_questions.question: Sunfrill Imitator attacks alongside Gishath and its attack trigger resolves, making it a copy of Gishath except for its name: does the copy have the combat-damage reveal trigger this combat, is it a 7/6 with vigilance, trample and haste, and does the legend rule ever apply given the names differ?
open_questions.why_it_matters: if it holds, the deck's ignition stage has a second copy of its single point of failure for {2}{G}, and the 'connection kit' target is measuring the wrong thing

open_questions.question: Eerie Interlude cast in response to a sweeper with Pantlaza, Garruk's Uprising, Vaultborn Tyrant, Earthshaker Dreadmaw and four other Dinosaurs: all return at the next end step as one event — how many Uprising and Vaultborn draws, how many Dreadmaw draws, and exactly one Pantlaza discover at which X?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the line is drawn dashed from protection into conversion; a pass would make Interlude the deck's best re-trigger and not just its insurance

open_questions.question: What board actually kills a 40-life opponent, and from how far? No checker-passed stack resolves a lethal swing; the closest measurement is stack 004's 16 redirected damage taking one opponent from 26 to 10.
open_questions.why_it_matters: every arrow into wincon is dashed, and the goldfish's kill-by-turn-8 of 0.617 is against one opponent with no blockers

open_questions.question: Re-resolve the enrage residue on a board this 99 can produce: Blasphemous Act through Temple Altisaur with Trapjaw Tyrant AND Wrathful Raptors on the table. Stack 004's board carries Ripjaw Raptor and stack 005's carries Forerunner, Ranging Raptors, Ripjaw and Polyraptor — none in the deck — and stacks 002 and 003 name zero current cards.
open_questions.why_it_matters: the per-card verified index still credits Trapjaw Tyrant to a board the deck cannot reach; a scenario the current list produces is what the page should cite

open_questions.question: How much of the conversion stage's draw does the model see? Vaultborn Tyrant and Curious Altisaur are named in draw_not_modelled, Rishkar's Expertise and Hunter's Insight are X-based, and the reveal's 4.096 free bodies a game is the arrival count those draws key off.
open_questions.why_it_matters: extra cards drawn by turn 8 reads 1.353; if the per-entry draws are dark, the stage that pays the reveal back is being measured as almost nothing

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Split: 'Command-zone discount drawn' (Otepec Huntmaster, Urza's Incubator, Knight of the Stampede) and 'Dinosaur cheated into play' (Descendants' Path, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual // Zoological Study, Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fifth People).
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: only the three reducers can make a command-zone cast cheaper; the other four put a Dinosaur onto the battlefield from hand or library and cannot touch Gishath. As declared the seven-card group reads 81.0% assembled, 64.1% by turn 6 (goldfish_metrics) for a question it half-answers.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: The Gishath connection kit (haste or evasion for the 7/6)
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Rescope to size-and-evasion on the attack: Rogue's Passage, Kessig Wolf Run, Enlarge, Overwhelming Stampede. Move Otepec Huntmaster and Regisaur Alpha to a separate 'haste for the arriving board' group if wanted. Consider a 'second reveal' group: Boros Charm (double strike), Huatli's Saga chapter IV, Sunfrill Imitator (pending the stack).
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Gishath's own oracle line is 'Vigilance, trample, haste'; a haste grant does nothing for the 7/6 the label names. Enlarge is the deck's largest single reveal multiplier and is in no target.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Add Vaultborn Tyrant and Earthshaker Dreadmaw.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: both are per-Dinosaur-entry triggers of exactly the kind the label describes; Dreadmaw is new to the list and Vaultborn has been in it since V3. Regisaur Alpha, which is in the group, is a haste grant plus one token.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Either pair the converters with a damage source as a two-group target — any of 'Blasphemous Act', 'Zacama, Primal Calamity', 'Itzquinth, Firstborn of Gishath', 'Trumpeting Carnosaur', 'Triumphant Chomp' AND any of 'Trapjaw Tyrant', 'Wrathful Raptors' — or retire it.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: it now measures two converters at 56.7% assembled with no damage source declared. Enumerated from cards.json, the deck marks damage on its own Dinosaurs five ways plus a blocker: Blasphemous Act (the only one-sided sweeper), Zacama's {2}{R} activation (Forge V3 activated it 32 times), Itzquinth's ETB, Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard mode and Triumphant Chomp, each of the last four aimed at your own Trapjaw or Wrathful at a removal spell's price. As labelled it describes an engine the V4 list no longer runs.
